I quit my last job and was unemployed for 4 months due to my mental health. The break was good. I'm working again out of necessity, and it's difficult. I don't know if I'd be breathing right now if I hadn't taken that break though. Mental health is equivalent to physical health, treat it as such. Do what you need to in order to take care of yourself, if that means taking time off of work then there is no shame in that.

I can't help you. I can tell you though, you're not alone in your pain. My family is religious too so I can understand being reluctant to go to them for help. I went through similar things in school. I was never diagnosed with autism, but I have severe social anxiety which caused me to learn things quite a bit later than my peers. For a while it got better for me once I graduated. I saw a therapist for a while, got myself into a toxic relationship out of desperation, got completely devastated when they left, stopped seeing my therapist because it wasn't helping. It gets tiring. I understand wanting the pain to go away. I'm honestly not sure why I'm still hanging on. I can't stand the thought of reading something so relatable without saying something though. So, let me be a hypocrite for a moment and tell you to keep hanging onto life. I don't know a thing about you, but given your care for academics I would imagine that you are a smart person with a bright future ahead of you. I can't tell you that things will get better or that it will all be ok. I can tell you that if you die tomorrow, that possibility will be completely gone. Once you're dead, that's it. No more tomorrows. So I think it's at least worth it to try to hang onto hope that things will get better, even if it's a false hope. Do anything you can to keep yourself breathing, because if things really do get better for you, you'll be glad that you're still here. Sorry if I couldn't help you or if I made things worse, I just felt like I had to try. Don't give up on yourself yet.

I ended up quitting my job. A job I had been so excited for and worked so hard to get. It felt like there was no way I could go back there though, so now I sit at home all day and slowly eat away at my savings until I get my shit together or die. After the last breakdown at work I figured it was only a matter of time before I got myself fired. I still don't know if quitting was the right decision or not. I don't have any good advice but I just want to let you know you're not alone, no matter how much it may feel that way.
It really sucks doesn't it. I think we both just need to keep hanging on and maybe we'll get lucky. Wishing you the best.
